activity.title: This past weekend, Adam Zeineldin , Reyan Yousif , Bassil Shalaby , and I built Immortal at Anthropic’s Hackathon and won Best Healthcare Hack. We were frustrated that wearables collect tons of health data but don’t actually help you do anything with it. You can see your HRV drop, but not why, what to change, or how to test it. So we built a closed-loop system that learns your personal baselines, detects meaningful changes, and turns them into evidence-backed recommendations with real citations. The part we’re most excited about is self-experiments. You can test something like cutting caffeine after 2pm, and Immortal will track the before and after, compute the effect, and tell you if it actually worked. We paired deterministic models for reliability with an LLM layer for personalized guidance, which ended up being a really strong combination. Super proud of how much we built in such a short time, and excited to keep pushing this forward. +1 Hackathon Win Devpost: https://lnkd.in/e2nRVv-h

Incredibly grateful to share that our team won 1st Place Overall and 1st Place in the Societal Impact track at YHack 2026! We built Circa a smart farming management system designed to tackle one of agriculture's most persistent problems: inefficient irrigation. Nearly 40–50% of water is wasted in traditional farming systems, and current solutions are expensive, hard to control, and spatially inefficient. Circa uses a network of ESP32-powered sensor nodes spread across a field, each collecting real-time soil moisture, temperature, and humidity data. That data feeds into a web dashboard where farmers can monitor their entire field, automate watering decisions, and control a central water turret, all from one place. The turret's design extends circular irrigation to rectangular fields, meaning less wasted space and far more precise water delivery. None of this would have happened without my incredible teammates: Dvij Raicha , Shanmukha Pothukuchi , and Abhinav Arora . Grateful to have had such a hardworking, creative, and mission-driven team by my side. Thank you to the organizers at YHack for creating such an amazing space for builders. Try a demo of our project at circaorg.github.io

Excited to announce I’ll be at Y Combinator ’s Startup School! I'd love to connect with anyone else going. Looking forward to meeting other founders and hearing from speakers like Jensen Huang, Sam Altman, Jeff Dean, and Alexandr Wang.

Apparently startup founders are getting older. This is terrible news. Who is going to keep the hoodie industry alive? Ever since dot-com we've been sold the image of the successful founder as a 23-year-old living on ramen, fueled by energy drinks and venture capital. The research says otherwise. When you look at the fastest-growing startups, the average founder is about 45 years old. Not 25. Forty-five. And honestly... that matches exactly what I see in Seattle. The average founder in the Venture Mechanics Catapult Accelerator is over 45, married with children. Many are "second-career" entrepreneurs who just left Microsoft, Amazon, Boeing, or another large company with something even more valuable than a severance package: 20-30 years of domain expertise. They're building AI infrastructure, enterprise software, robotics, aerospace, defense, climate tech, healthcare, and industrial systems—the kinds of companies where experience compounds instead of depreciates. Turns out spending a couple of decades learning how an industry is broken is pretty good preparation for fixing it. Maybe that's why the stereotype has it backwards. Your 20s are for learning. Your 30s are for mastering. Your 40s are when you finally know which problems are actually worth solving. So if you're in your 40s or 50s wondering whether you missed your chance to build a startup... ...you may have just aged into your competitive advantage. One question for the 40+ crowd: If your resume and your severance package were your seed round... what would you build?

🛰️ Meet Circa — a precision irrigation platform powered by K2 Think V2 that lets any grower, in any language, apply true precision watering to their fields. Why focus on farming? Agriculture accounts for roughly 70% of global freshwater use. Circular irrigation saves water compared to traditional rectangular methods, but leaves the land in the corners underused. Circa’s hardware addresses both: a directional turret with full X/Y/Z control, paired with moisture-sensing nodes that tell the system exactly where and when water is needed. The result is irrigation that responds to what the soil actually needs, not a fixed schedule. The software layer handles live sensor data, manual targeting, automated sweeps, and ML-powered soil moisture forecasts — with an AI assistant powered by K2 Think V2 at its center. Farmers do not need to learn a complex interface to water their crops. Using K2 Think V2, the Circa team lets each grower describe what they want in plain language; the model parses intent, extracts parameters (zone, threshold, duration), and creates live automation rules the system executes. What makes this stand out: ✨ Natural-language rule creation that executes directly — no interface learning curve. ✨ Live soil moisture sensing with ML-powered forecasting from distributed field nodes. ✨ Multilingual input designed in, not bolted on. Watch the case study below to hear from the Circa team themselves! #K2Think #MBZUAI #IFM #YHack #Hackathon
